question: Which of the following is formed by the action of chlorine on dry slaked lime?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Bleaching powder**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Bleaching powder is chemically known as **Calcium hypochlorite** (Ca(OCl)₂).
 
• It is formed by the action of chlorine gas on dry **slaked lime** (Ca(OH)₂).
 
• The chemical reaction is: Ca(OH)₂ + Cl₂ → Ca(OCl)₂ + H₂O.
 
• Bleaching powder is used as a disinfectant and a bleaching agent due to its strong oxidizing properties.
 
• It is commonly used in water treatment plants to purify drinking water.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Calcium Oxide (CaO)**

 
 
• Also known as quicklime, it is produced by heating limestone (CaCO₃) in a kiln.
 
• Calcium oxide reacts with water to form slaked lime (Ca(OH)₂).
 
 
 
• **Hydrochloric Acid (HCl)**
 
 
• A strong acid that is commonly used in industrial and laboratory settings.
 
• It is produced by dissolving hydrogen chloride gas in water.
 
 
 
• **Calcium Chloride (CaCl₂)**
 
 
• It is a salt used for de-icing roads and as a drying agent due to its hygroscopic properties.
 
• Calcium chloride can be produced by neutralizing hydrochloric acid with calcium carbonate.
